questions.question: Explain what a PAT is and describe what the Grade 8 Term 1 PAT requires a team to produce.
questions.expected_answer: A PAT is a Practical Assessment Task, the main formal assessment of the term, in which learners investigate, design, make, evaluate and communicate a solution to a stated problem, working in teams but each keeping a portfolio of evidence. The Term 1 PAT requires a structure that houses a mechanism: a stable, stiff frame that stands, carries a load and protects a crank-driven mechanism using gears, a cam, a wheel and axle, a pulley or a lever, built as a working model from simple materials to solve a community scenario such as a hand-powered bucket lift or barrier.

questions.question: Map the five IDMEC steps onto the weeks of the term and state one piece of portfolio evidence for each step.
questions.expected_answer: Investigate, Weeks 4-5: notes and labelled sketches of existing structures (pylons, bridges) and mechanisms with advantages and disadvantages. Design, Week 6: design brief with specifications and constraints, initial idea sketches, chosen idea with reasons, single-view 2D working drawing. Make, Week 7: the model and photographs of the stages. Evaluate, Week 8: completed evaluation sheet testing the model against each specification. Communicate, Week 9: the class presentation of plans, model and evaluation (Week 10 adds the isometric drawing).

questions.question: Explain how the structural and mechanical parts of the PAT model depend on each other and where they meet, and describe the model using input, process and output.
questions.expected_answer: The frame must be stable (wide base, low centre of gravity) and stiff (triangulated) or the mechanism will skip or jam when the crank is turned; the mechanism needs axles passing through aligned holes in frame members, so the frame must be designed around the axle positions. They meet at the bearings, where axles pass through the frame; holes must be neither too tight nor too loose and the members reinforced there. Input: a person turning the crank. Process: the gears, cam, pulley or lever inside the frame. Output: the lifted bucket, raised barrier or moving display.
